review_notes: Normative orthography contract for the project's ku-Latn target. The letter set is the project's explicit alphabet policy (data-builder/src/alphabet.rs).

Human review of 2026-09-19 (project owner): the alphabet reference is Bedir Khan & Lescot, Grammaire kurde (dialecte kurmandji), Part I §2, p. 3, and the casing reference is Unicode default case mapping (The Unicode Standard, Version 18.0.0) with no Turkish-specific dotted or dotless i tailoring for ku-Latn; both selected and approved by the owner and recorded in `references`.

Word-internal hyphen and apostrophes are governed by the word-punctuation policy of 2026-09-19 (docs/lexicon-review.md): such forms are held for linguist review and are not in the default pack; the contract itself still neither admits nor forbids them as letters.
alphabet_basis: The 31-letter Kurmancî Latin alphabet, identical to the project's default-pack alphabet policy, the seed vocabulary, the review identities and the engine normalization.

references.supports: the project's 31-letter inventory a b c ç d e ê f g h i î j k l m n o p q r s ş t u û v w x y z
references.source_statement: Part I, §2 lists these 31 core characters and states that there are 33 if two optional characters are added. The project's production alphabet is exactly the 31-letter policy; the optional characters are not added, and this qualification is recorded as a finding, not a change.
references.work: Bedir Khan, Djeladet; Lescot, Roger. Grammaire kurde (dialecte kurmandji)
references.edition: Paris: Librairie d'Amérique et d'Orient Adrien Maisonneuve, 1970

references.supports: the casing pairs of this contract: Unicode default casing, i ↔ I only; no Turkish-specific dotted or dotless i tailoring is applied to ku-Latn
references.source_statement: Default case conversion and the simple case mappings of the Unicode Character Database; locale-specific tailorings (such as the Turkish and Azeri dotted/dotless i rules) are not applied to ku-Latn.
references.location: §3.13 Default Case Algorithms; §5.18 Case Mappings; Unicode Character Database, UnicodeData.txt (simple case mappings)

distinct_letters_note: ç ê î ş û are distinct Kurmancî alphabet letters, not interchangeable representations of c e i s u. Their canonical Unicode decompositions (base letter plus combining mark) are an encoding property; orthographic letter identity is separate, and replacing one with its base letter changes the word. A base-letter ↔ distinct-letter change proposed by spell correction is a linguistic correction, never an equivalence.

notes: Casing is locale-independent Unicode default casing: 'i' pairs only with 'I' (U+0049) and 'I' only with 'i' (U+0069). A host must never apply another locale's dotted or dotless i rules to ku-Latn text.
Sentence-initial and title capitalization keep the letter's identity: 'êvar' → 'Êvar', 'şev' → 'Şev'.

normalization.reference: engine normalize(): Unicode control characters, U+200B and U+FEFF removed, then NFC, then lowercase; identical to the repository's canonical review identity rule (normalize_text)
notes: Precomposed letters and base letter plus combining mark are the same text: 's' + U+0327 and 'ş' normalize to the same word.
Ordinary whitespace and NBSP are not stripped; the host tokenizes on whitespace before querying the engine.

not_covered_by_this_contract: Word-internal hyphen and apostrophes ('-', U+0027, U+2019): not letters; whether and how they occur inside words is the word-punctuation policy (project owner, 2026-09-19, docs/lexicon-review.md), under which such forms are held for linguist review and are not in the default pack. This contract neither admits nor forbids them.

Digits and other punctuation and symbols, excluding the held word-punctuation characters described above ('-', U+0027, U+2019), are not alphabet letters and not lexical characters; their keyboard layers follow host conventions. Whether the held characters are ultimately lexical is not decided here.
Characters observed in source data that are outside the alphabet: source-quality findings recorded by the generated alphabet audit (data-builder audit-alphabet), never part of this contract.
